function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
Java is a high‑level, class‑based, object‑oriented programming language that was originally developed by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems (now owned by Oracle Corporation). It was designed with the following core principles in mind:

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Platform‑independent** | Java code is compiled into bytecode, which runs on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM). Because the JVM abstracts away the underlying hardware and operating system, the same program can run on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and many other platforms without modification. |
| **Object‑oriented** | Everything in Java is an object (except primitive types). This encourages modular design, encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism. |
| **Strongly typed** | Variables must be declared with a specific type, and the compiler checks type compatibility at compile time, reducing runtime errors. |
| **Automatic memory management** | Java uses garbage collection to reclaim memory from objects that are no longer reachable, freeing developers from manual memory deallocation. |
| **Rich standard library** | The Java Standard Edition (SE) provides extensive APIs for collections, networking, I/O, concurrency, GUI (Swing, JavaFX), and more. |
| **Security** | The JVM sandbox, bytecode verification, and security manager help protect against malicious code. |
| **Multithreading support** | Java has built‑in support for concurrent execution via threads, executors, and higher‑level concurrency utilities. |

### Typical Use Cases

| Domain | Common Java Applications |
|--------|--------------------------|
| **Enterprise software** | Backend services, web applications (Servlets, JSP, Spring), microservices |
| **Android development** | Native Android apps (though Kotlin is now preferred) |
| **Desktop applications** | Swing, JavaFX, or cross‑platform UI frameworks |
| **Big data & analytics** | Hadoop, Spark (written in Scala but interoperable with Java) |
| **Embedded systems** | Java ME (Micro Edition) for devices with limited resources |
| **Financial services** | High‑frequency trading platforms, risk analysis tools |

### Key Ecosystem Components

| Component | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| **JDK (Java Development Kit)** | Includes the compiler (`javac`), JVM, and core libraries. |
| **JRE (Java Runtime Environment)** | Provides the JVM and core libraries needed to run Java programs. |
| **Build tools** | Maven, Gradle, Ant – manage dependencies, build lifecycle, and packaging. |
| **IDE** | IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, NetBeans – provide code completion, debugging, refactoring. |
| **Frameworks** | Spring, Jakarta EE, Hibernate, Micronaut – simplify enterprise development. |

### Quick Example

```java
public class HelloWorld {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("Hello, world!");
    }
}
```

Compile with `javac HelloWorld.java`, then run with `java HelloWorld`. The output will be `Hello, world!`.

---

In short, Java is a versatile, mature language that powers a wide range of software—from mobile apps to large‑scale enterprise systems—thanks to its portability, robust ecosystem, and strong emphasis on safety and performance.
